text: The applicant was born in 1954.
The applicant lives in Engelskirchen, Germany.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 7 April 2002 (first round) legislative elections took place in Hungary.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 21 April 2002 (second round) legislative elections took place in Hungary.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The coalition which had governed Hungary from 1998 had been in charge of organising the April 2002 legislative elections.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The coalition which had governed Hungary from 1998 lost their majority in the April 2002 legislative elections.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The official results of the April 2002 elections were established by the local and regional electoral commissions following the second round.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: After the courts had ruled on certain complaints concerning the legality and outcome of the voting procedure, on 4 May 2002 the National Election Committee made a public statement in the Official Gazette.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: According to the National Election Committee's public statement in the Official Gazette on 4 May 2002, the result of the April 2002 elections had become final.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The final results of the April 2002 elections were virtually identical to the results of the exit poll carried out on the day of the second round (21 April 2002), as had been the case in previous Hungarian elections.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The final results of the April 2002 elections were virtually identical to the preliminary results announced by the National Election Committee on the evening of 21 April 2002, as had been the case in previous Hungarian elections.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: Views were subsequently voiced in certain sections of the media that the April 2002 elections had been "rigged".
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: International observers, in particular the Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), found that the April 2002 parliamentary elections in Hungary had been conducted in a manner consistent with international standards.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) found that the Hungarian election system had provided the basis for a generally transparent, accountable, free, fair and equal process in the April 2002 parliamentary elections.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: A period of two months elapsed after the April 2002 elections during which a new government was formed in a coalition of the ex-opposition parties.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The new coalition government of ex-opposition parties took up its functions on 27 May 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On the morning of Thursday, 4 July 2002, several hundred demonstrators started to protest against the statutory destruction of the ballots from the April 2002 elections, which was scheduled for 20 to 22 July 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On the morning of 4 July 2002, the demonstrators blocked the centrally located Erzsébet Bridge in Budapest with their cars.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The objective of the demonstrators who blocked Erzsébet Bridge on 4 July 2002 was to force a recount of the April 2002 election votes.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The demonstrators who blocked Erzsébet Bridge on 4 July 2002 brought traffic to a complete standstill.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The demonstrators who blocked Erzsébet Bridge on 4 July 2002 had not given prior notice of their gathering to the police, as required by Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act).
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The demonstration at Erzsébet Bridge on the morning of 4 July 2002 was dispersed after several hours.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: Shortly after the dispersal of the Erzsébet Bridge demonstration, at around 1 p.m. on 4 July 2002, more demonstrators assembled at Kossuth Square in front of the Parliament building in Budapest.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The demonstrators who assembled at Kossuth Square at around 1 p.m. on 4 July 2002 did so without any prior notification to the police.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The demonstrators at Kossuth Square on 4 July 2002 demanded a recount of the April 2002 election votes.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The demonstrators at Kossuth Square on 4 July 2002 expressed their support for the participants in the morning's events at Erzsébet Bridge.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: According to the applicant's submissions of 14 February 2005 and the Government's observations, the demonstrators at Kossuth Square on 4 July 2002 had been at the Erzsébet Bridge and then relocated to Kossuth Square.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: In her submissions of 23 December 2007, the applicant stated that the demonstrators at Kossuth Square on 4 July 2002 had merely been supporters of those who had blocked the Erzsébet Bridge, rather than the same individuals.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: Having learnt of the events at Kossuth Square from the news, the applicant joined the demonstration at Kossuth Square at around 7 p.m. on 4 July 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: By the time the applicant joined the demonstration at Kossuth Square at around 7 p.m. on 4 July 2002, traffic and public transport — including the circulation of trams and trolley-buses — had become seriously disrupted in the area of Kossuth Square.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The estimated number of demonstrators at Kossuth Square on 4 July 2002 ranged from several hundred to two or three thousand.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The police initially attempted to allow the circulation of traffic to continue during the Kossuth Square demonstration on 4 July 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The police eventually had to close some streets nearby Kossuth Square during the demonstration on 4 July 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: Faced with an unmanageable situation, the police broke up the Kossuth Square demonstration at about 9 p.m. on 4 July 2002 without using any force.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicant participated in the Kossuth Square demonstration on 4 July 2002 until it was dispersed at about 9 p.m.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Hungarian media reported in detail on the events of 4 July 2002, and the affair was the leading news in the country.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: In an official communiqué, the President of the Republic of Hungary condemned the events of 4 July 2002, declaring them illegal.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: In his official communiqué, the President of the Republic of Hungary underlined that Hungary was a stable parliamentary democracy where human rights were observed and where even critical views should be voiced in a lawful manner.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicant sought judicial review of the actions of the police before the Budapest Central District Court.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicant asserted before the Budapest Central District Court that the dispersal of the Kossuth Square demonstration on 4 July 2002 had been unlawful.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 1 October 2003 the Budapest Central District Court dismissed the applicant's claim.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Central District Court established that the duty to inform the police about planned assemblies was applicable to every type of demonstration, including spontaneous ones.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicant did not deny that the Kossuth Square demonstration on 4 July 2002 had not been notified to the police, as required by section 14 of Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act).
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Central District Court found that, since the Kossuth Square demonstration had not been notified to the police as required by section 14 of the Assembly Act, the police had not had any other choice but to break it up.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Central District Court found that the duty to inform the police in advance about assemblies held in public served the protection of the public interest and the rights of others, namely the prevention of disorder and the undisturbed circulation of traffic.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Central District Court concluded that the measures taken by the police in dispersing the Kossuth Square demonstration on 4 July 2002 had been in compliance with the law.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicant appealed against the Budapest Central District Court's decision of 1 October 2003.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 13 July 2004 the Budapest Regional Court upheld the first-instance decision of the Budapest Central District Court dismissing the applicant's claim.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Regional Court's judgment of 13 July 2004 was served on the applicant's lawyer on 31 August 2004.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: Article 62 of the Constitution of the Republic of Hungary (Act no. 20 of 1949 as amended) provides: "The Republic of Hungary acknowledges the right to peaceful assembly and secures its free exercise."
section_path: 1.  The Constitution of the Republic of Hungary

text: Section 2(3) of Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act) provides that the exercise of freedom of assembly shall not constitute a crime or an incitement to crime, and moreover, it should not result in the infringement of the rights and freedoms of others.
section_path: 2.  Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly

text: Section 6 of Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act) provides that the organisation of an event held in the public domain shall be notified to the competent police headquarters according to the place of the event, and in Budapest to the Budapest Police Headquarters, three days prior to the planned date of the event, and that the obligation to notify the police lies with the organiser of the event.
section_path: 2.  Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly

text: Section 8(1) of Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act), as in force at the relevant time, provides that if the holding of an event subject to prior notification seriously endangers the proper functioning of the representative bodies or courts, or results in a disproportionate hindrance of the circulation of traffic, the police may ban the holding of the event at the place or time indicated in the notification, within 48 hours from the receipt of the notification by the authority.
section_path: 2.  Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly

text: Section 9(1) of Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act) provides that no appeal shall lie against the decision of the police, but the organiser may seek judicial review of the administrative decision within three days of its notification.
section_path: 2.  Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly

text: Section 14(1) of Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act), as in force at the relevant time, provides that the police shall disperse an event if the exercise of the right to freedom of assembly contravenes section 2(3) of the Assembly Act, or if the participants appear at the event in possession of arms, or if an event subject to prior notification is held without notification, or despite a decision banning the event.
section_path: 2.  Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly

text: Section 14(3) of Act no. 3 of 1989 on Freedom of Assembly (the Assembly Act), as in force at the relevant time, provides that if an event is dispersed, the participants may seek judicial review within fifteen days with a view to the establishment of the illegality of the dispersal.
